newsitem.title: USA: House approves breast cancer research stamp.
newsitem.headline: House approves breast cancer research stamp.

text.p: The House voted 422-3 late Tuesday to approve a measure creating a breast cancer postage stamp to help fund research into the disease.
The stamp could be sold with a surcharge of up to 8 cents above the normal first-class postage -- currently 32 cents -- with the extra money to be earmarked for breast cancer research.
The Post Office had opposed creating a stamp to raise money for one specific cause, but lawmakers argued that it made sense to raise money for research on the deadly disease.
The Senate approved similar legislation last week, although that bill would limit the surcharge to one cent over the rate for a first-class letter.
Lawmakers will have to reconcile the two versions.

The House bill would funnel 70 percent of the revenues generated by sale of the new stamp to fund National Institutes of Health research on breast cancer, with 30 percent going to Defence Department studies.

The House bill's chief sponsor, Representative Susan Molinari, a New York Republican, has predicted that millions of people will happily pay a few extra pennies for stamps to support the research efforts.

During last week's debate in the Senate, Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, said if 10 percent of first class stamps sold each year were purchased at the higher rate, the Senate measure would raise $60 million for research.
